newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary central bank assets, profit drop in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hungary central bank assets, profit drop in 1996.

text.p: The balance sheet total of the National Bank of Hungary fell to 5,119.3 billion forints in 1996 from 5,420.4 billion, while its pre-tax profits dropped to 2.46 billion from 6.6 billion in 1995, the NBH said on Friday.
The NBH said in a statement that its balance sheet total dropped mainly due to the spending of Hungary's privatisation revenues for reducing the country's foreign debt.

The NBH's foreign currency and gold reserves dropped to $9.7 billion by December 31, 1996, from 12 billion at the end of 1995 as soaring privatisation revenues at end-1995 and early 1996 were parked In the reserve account before being spent on debt repayment, the NBH said.
The NBH's net foreign currency debt dropped by $4.5 billion in 1996 to $12.87 billion.

Relatively high forint interest rates and the creation of convertibility for the forint on January 1 for current account transactions encouraged a drop in foreign currency deposits of banks with the NBH and boosted forint deposits, the NBH said.

These foreign currency deposits fell by 161.2 billion forints in 1996, while the forint deposits rose by 232.3 billion, with forint funds kept in the reverse repo facilities rising substantially, the NBH said.

Throughout 1996, the forint was usually pinned to the resistance level of the NBH's 4.5 percent wide floating intervention range and the NBH increased Hungary's forint liquidity by buying substantial amounts of foreign currencies.
However, the NBH ensured a balanced market by taking up deposits in the reverse repo facilities, thus counteracting the increase in forint liquidity, the central bank said.
Due to the increase in funds kept in the reverse repo facilities, the NBH's interest expenditures rose by 39 billion forints in 1996, the NBH said.
